description: Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani, is a world-renowned Indian dish celebrated for its rich, creamy, and mildly spiced tomato gravy. This classic recipe features succulent pieces of chicken enveloped in an aromatic sauce, making it a truly comforting and luxurious meal. It is a perfect choice for an authentic Indian lunch that is both satisfying and flavorful.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 min

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 0.5 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary, and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the remaining 0.5 teaspoon garam masala, and soaked cashews. Add a splash of water if the mixture is too thick. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon stick.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky sauce, you can strain it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step ensures no bits of onion or cashew remain.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the blended sauce to the pan over low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, crushed Kasuri Methi, and sugar (if using). Stir well to combine. Simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce. Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Heat through gently, but do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve your authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with naan bread, basmati rice, or roti.

tips: For a deeper flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful it becomes.
Do not skip blending and straining the sauce. This is key to achieving the signature silky smooth texture of restaurant-style Butter Chicken.

Adjust the level of spice by increasing or decreasing the Kashmiri red chili powder. For a richer color without much heat, use more Kashmiri chili. For extra heat, add a pinch of regular red chili powder.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: The Quintessential Indian Lunch Recipe

When it comes to the world of Indian cuisine, few dishes evoke as much warmth, comfort, and sheer deliciousness as Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its creamy texture, rich tomato-based gravy, and succulent pieces of chicken, has captivated palates across the globe. Perfectly balanced between sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is not just a meal; it's an experience, making it an ideal candidate for a satisfying and memorable Indian lunch. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the vibrant flavors of India, mastering this dish is a rewarding culinary journey.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter," a name that hints at the luxurious richness that defines this dish. Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, where it was created almost by accident as a way to use leftover tandoori chicken. The chefs developed a rich, creamy tomato sauce, simmered with butter, cream, and a blend of aromatic spices, to tenderize and flavor the chicken. The result was an immediate sensation.

At its heart, Butter Chicken is characterized by tender pieces of boneless chicken (often marinated in yogurt and spices and then grilled or pan-fried) swimming in a velvety smooth sauce. The sauce itself is a complex symphony of flavors, built upon a base of pureed tomatoes, onions, ginger, and garlic. Cashews or almonds are often added to provide body and an extra layer of creaminess. The generous use of butter (makhan) and fresh cream gives the sauce its signature silken texture and mild, slightly sweet taste, which is beautifully complemented by the subtle bitterness of dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) and the warmth of garam masala. It’s a dish that masterfully balances acidity from the tomatoes with sweetness from cream and a hint of sugar, creating an utterly irresistible flavor profile perfect for an indulgent Indian lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients, each playing a crucial role in building its layered flavors.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   **Chicken:** Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces, are ideal. Thighs tend to stay juicier.
*   **Yogurt:** Plain, full-fat yogurt helps tenderize the chicken and allows spices to adhere.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** A foundational flavor in Indian cooking.
*   **Spices:** Red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color), turmeric, garam masala, cumin powder, and salt.

For the Rich Makhani Sauce:
*   **Butter:** Unsalted butter is key for that signature richness.
*   **Onions:** Finely chopped or pureed.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** Again, essential for depth.
*   **Tomatoes:** Canned crushed tomatoes, tomato puree, or fresh ripe tomatoes pureed. They form the backbone of the sauce.
*   **Cashews:** Soaked cashews, pureed, contribute to the sauce's thickness and creamy texture.
*   **Green Chilies:** Optional, for a touch of heat.
*   **Spices:** Garam masala, red chili powder, and a pinch of turmeric.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** This is a non-negotiable ingredient, providing a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor.
*   **Heavy Cream:** For that luxurious finish and to mellow the flavors.
*   **Sugar:** A small amount helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes.
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Water or Chicken Broth:** To adjust sauce consistency.
*   **Fresh Cilantro:** For garnish.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

While making Butter Chicken may seem complex, breaking it down into steps makes it manageable and enjoyable.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and all marinade spices. Mix well and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably several hours in the refrigerator.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** You can grill, broil, pan-fry, or even bake the marinated chicken until it's cooked through and slightly charred. This step adds a crucial smoky depth, mimicking the tandoor oven.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In a large pot or karahi, melt butter. Sauté onions until softened, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using). Cook until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Cashews:** Stir in the pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews, and the sauce spices. Cook this mixture, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the sides, indicating the tomatoes are well cooked.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender and blend until it's perfectly smooth and silky. For an exceptionally smooth sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve.
6.  **Combine and Simmer:** Return the blended sauce to the pot. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. Add water or broth to achieve your desired consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer.
7.  **Finish with Cream and Kasoori Methi:** Stir in the heavy cream, sugar, and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
8.  **Garnish:** Garnish generously with fresh cilantro before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Sear the Chicken:** Whether you grill, broil, or pan-fry, get a good sear or char on the chicken. This adds a smoky depth that elevates the final dish.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A truly great Murgh Makhani sauce is incredibly smooth. Invest time in blending the sauce base thoroughly. Straining it through a sieve after blending ensures no lumps.
*   **Use Good Quality Ingredients:** Fresh, ripe tomatoes (or good quality canned tomatoes), high-fat butter, and heavy cream make a noticeable difference in the final taste and texture of your Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your sauce as you go. The balance between sweet, tangy, and spicy is crucial. A pinch of sugar can cut the acidity of tomatoes, while a little extra cream can mellow heat.
*   **Toast Kasoori Methi:** Lightly toast the kasoori methi in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing it between your palms and adding it to the sauce. This intensifies its aroma.
*   **Low and Slow Simmer:** After combining the chicken and sauce, let it simmer gently. This allows the flavors to fully develop and meld together beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a rich and hearty dish, and its accompaniments should complement its luxurious nature without overpowering it.

*   **Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan bread (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is the classic choice, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the delicious sauce. Tandoori roti or laccha paratha are also excellent options.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lighter counterpoint to the rich gravy.
*   **Sides:** A simple raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) or a fresh green salad with sliced onions can offer a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken. Pickled onions are also a fantastic addition.
*   **For Lunch:** This dish makes for a very satisfying and filling Indian lunch. Pack it in an insulated container with some naan or rice for a delightful midday meal.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, there are many ways to adapt it to your dietary preferences or ingredient availability:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** For a meat-free version, replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese) for Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, cauliflower, or mixed vegetables.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder and green chilies to suit your preference. For less heat, use Kashmiri chili powder, which provides color without much spice.
*   **Healthier Twist:** To reduce calories, use less butter and cream, or substitute with low-fat yogurt and milk (though the texture will be different). You can also grill or bake the chicken without any added oil.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews or substitute them with an equal amount of melon seeds or poppy seeds (soaked and pureed) for thickening, or simply use a little cornstarch slurry.
*   **Tomato Type:** While canned crushed tomatoes offer convenience, using fresh, ripe Roma tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and pureed, can impart a slightly fresher flavor.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani stands as a testament to the richness and diversity of Indian cuisine. Its enduring popularity as a beloved Indian lunch recipe is no surprise, given its comforting flavors and satisfying texture. Whether you're making it for a special occasion or a simple weekday meal, this dish promises a delightful culinary experience that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of India. Embrace the butter, savor the cream, and enjoy the magic of this truly iconic dish.
